<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are not currently aware of any non-compliance with any state or federal statute, rule, or regulation which we believe would have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, or financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Environmental Matters</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.</font> Under various federal, state, and local environmental laws, ordinances, and regulations, a current or previous owner or operator of real estate may be required to investigate and clean up hazardous or toxic substances or petroleum product releases at such property, and may be held liable to a governmental entity or to third parties for property damage and tort liability and for investigation and clean-up costs incurred by such parties in connection with the contamination.&#160;&#160;Such laws typically impose clean-up responsibility and liability without regard to whether the owner or operator knew of or caused the presence of the contaminants, and the liability under such laws has been interpreted to be joint and several unless the harm is divisible and there is a reasonable basis for allocation of responsibility.&#160;&#160;The cost of investigation, remediation, or removal of such substances may be substantial, and the presence of such substances, or the failure to properly remediate the contamination on such property, may adversely affect the owner's ability to sell such property or to borrow using such property as collateral.&#160;&#160;Persons who arrange for the disposal or treatment of hazardous or toxic substances at a disposal or treatment facility also may be liable for the costs of removal or remediation of a release of hazardous or toxic substances at such disposal or treatment facility, whether or not such facility is owned or operated by such person.&#160;&#160;In addition, some environmental laws create a lien on the contaminated site in favor of the government for damages and costs it incurs in connection with the contamination.&#160;&#160;Finally, the owner or operator of a site may be subject to common law claims by third parties based on damages and costs resulting from environmental contamination emanating from a site or from environmental regulatory violations.&#160;&#160;In connection with our ownership and operation of our properties, we may be potentially liable for such claims.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and ordinances govern the removal, encapsulation, or disturbance of asbestos-containing materials (&#8220;ACMs&#8221;) when such materials are in poor condition or in the event of construction, remodeling, renovation, or demolition of a building.&#160;&#160;Such laws may impose liability for release of ACMs and may provide for third parties to seek recovery from owners or operators of real properties for personal injury associated with ACMs.&#160;&#160;In connection with our ownership and operation of our properties, we may be potentially liable for such costs.&#160;&#160;In 2001, we conducted a limited asbestos survey at each of our resorts existing at that time, which did not reveal material potential losses associated with ACMs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition, studies have linked radon, a naturally occurring substance, to increased risks of lung cancer.&#160;&#160;While there are currently no state or federal requirements regarding the monitoring for, presence of, or exposure to radon in indoor air, the EPA and the Surgeon General recommend testing residences for the presence of radon in indoor air.&#160;&#160;The EPA further recommends that concentrations of radon in indoor air be limited to less than 4 picocuries per liter of air (Pci/L) (the &#8220;Recommended Action Level&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The presence of radon in concentrations equal to or greater than the Recommended Action Level in one or more of our properties may adversely affect our ability to sell Vacation Intervals at such properties and the market value of such property.&#160;&#160;We have not tested our properties for radon.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Electric transmission lines are located in the vicinity of some of our properties.&#160;&#160;Electric transmission lines are one of many sources of electromagnetic fields (&#8220;EMFs&#8221;) to which people may be exposed.&#160;&#160;Research into potential health impacts associated with exposure to EMFs has produced inconclusive results.&#160;&#160;Notwithstanding the lack of conclusive scientific evidence, some states now regulate the strength of electric and magnetic fields emanating from electric transmission lines, while others have required transmission facilities to measure for levels of EMFs.&#160;&#160;In addition, we understand that lawsuits have, on occasion, been filed (primarily against electric utilities) alleging personal injuries resulting from exposure as well as fear of adverse health effects.&#160;&#160;In addition, fear of adverse health effects from transmission lines has been a factor considered in determining property value in obtaining financing and in condemnation and eminent domain proceedings brought by power companies seeking to construct transmission lines.&#160;&#160;Therefore, potential exists for the value of a property to be adversely affected as a result of its proximity to a transmission line and for the Company to be exposed to damage claims by persons exposed to EMFs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We conducted Phase I environmental assessments at each of our resorts during 2001 or later to identify potential environmental concerns.&#160;&#160;These Phase I assessments were carried out in accordance with accepted industry practices and consisted of non-invasive investigations of environmental conditions at the properties, including a preliminary investigation of the sites and identification of publicly known conditions concerning properties in the vicinity of the sites, physical site inspections, review of aerial photographs and relevant governmental records where readily available, interviews with knowledgeable parties, investigation for the presence of above-ground and underground storage tanks presently or formerly at the sites, and the preparation and issuance of written reports.&#160;&#160;Our Phase I assessments of the properties did not reveal any environmental liability that we believe would have a material adverse effect on our business, assets, or results of operations taken as a whole; nor are we aware of any such material environmental liability.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, it is possible that our Phase I assessments did not reveal all environmental liabilities or that there are material environmental liabilities of which we are unaware.&#160;&#160;Moreover, there can be no assurance that (i) future laws, ordinances, or regulations will not impose any material environmental liability or (ii) the current environmental condition of the properties will not be affected by the condition of land or operations in the vicinity of the properties (such as the presence of underground storage tanks) or by third parties unrelated to us.&#160;&#160;We do not believe that compliance with applicable environmental laws or regulations will have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity, or financial position.</font></div>

inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other Regulation. </font>Under various state and federal laws governing housing and places of public accommodation, including ADA, we are required to meet certain requirements related to access and use by disabled persons.&#160;&#160;Although we believe that our facilities are generally in compliance with present requirements of such laws, we are aware of certain of our properties that are not in full compliance with all aspects of such laws.&#160;&#160;We are presently responding, and expect to respond in the future, to inquiries, claims, and concerns from consumers and regulators regarding our compliance with existing state and federal regulations affording the disabled access to housing and accommodations.&#160;&#160;It is our practice to respond positively to all such inquiries, claims, and concerns and to work with regulators and consumers to resolve all issues arising under existing regulations concerning access and use of our properties by disabled persons.&#160;&#160;We believe that we will incur additional costs of compliance and/or remediation in the future with regard to the requirements of such existing regulations.&#160;&#160;Future legislation may also impose new or further burdens or restrictions on owners of timeshare resort properties with respect to access by the disabled.&#160;&#160;The ultimate cost of compliance with such legislation and/or remediation of conditions found to be non-compliant is not currently ascertainable, and while such costs are not expected to have a material effect on our business, such costs could be substantial.&#160;&#160;Limitations or restrictions on the completion of certain renovations may limit application of our growth strategy in certain instances or reduce profit margins on our operations.&#160;&#160;We are also subject to a variety of local, state, and federal laws and regulations concerning health and sanitation, facility operations, fire safety, and occupational safety.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Employees</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2009, we had 1,866 full and part-time employees and the Clubs collectively had 962 full and part-time employees.&#160;&#160;Our employee relations are good, both at the Company and at the Clubs.&#160;&#160;None of our employees are represented by a labor union and we are not aware of any union organization efforts with respect to any of our employees.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Insurance</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We carry comprehensive liability, fire, hurricane, and storm insurance with respect to our resorts, with policy specifications, insured limits, and deductibles customarily carried for similar properties, which we believe are adequate.&#160;&#160;However, certain types of losses (such as losses arising from floods in non-floodplain areas and acts of war) generally are not insured because such losses are either uninsurable or not economically insurable.&#160;&#160;Should an uninsured loss or a loss in excess of insured limits occur, we could lose the capital invested in a resort, as well as the anticipated future revenues from such resort, and would continue to be obligated on any mortgage indebtedness or other obligations related to the property.&#160;&#160;Any such loss could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity, or financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On September 13, 2008, Hurricane Ike caused property damage and business interruption related to our Seaside Resort in Galveston, Texas, and our Piney Shores Resort just north of Houston, Texas.&#160;&#160;As a result, Seaside Resort was closed from September 10 through October 17, 2008, at which time we began taking reservations and gradually opening units.&#160;&#160;The resort was fully operational by December 12, 2008.&#160;&#160;Piney Shores Resort was closed from September 13 to September 25, 2008.&#160;&#160;We maintain insurance that covers both physical damage and business-interruption losses.&#160;&#160;In 2008, we accrued $291,000 related to this incident, which represented our insurance deductibles and expenditures deemed uncollectible.&#160;&#160;No additional expenses related to this incident were incurred during 2009. In addition, in November 2008, we received $1.3 million in business-interruption proceeds, which was recorded in other income. In February 2009 and April 2009, we received $1.5 million and $879,000 in business-interruption proceeds, respectively, which were recorded in other income at the time of receipt.&#160;&#160;The April proceeds were received upon completion of our assessment of the full extent of business-interruption losses related to this hurricane.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We self-insure for employee medical claims reduced by certain stop-loss provisions.&#160;&#160;We also self-insure for property damage to certain vehicles and heavy equipment.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our senior credit facilities discussed above provide certain financial covenants that we must satisfy.&#160;&#160;Any failure to comply with the financial covenants in any single loan agreement will result in a cross default under the various facilities.&#160;&#160;As of and for the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009, we have been in full compliance with our debt covenants in our credit facilities with all of our senior lenders.&#160;&#160;Financial covenants existing at December 31, 2009 are described below.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Tangible Net Worth Covenant.&#160;&#160;</font>Although our senior lenders&#8217; requirements vary, the most restrictive &#8220;net worth&#8221; covenant is that we must maintain Tangible Net Worth at all times greater than the Tangible Net Worth as of December 31, 2004, or $132.1 million, plus 50% of the aggregate Consolidated Net Income after December 31, 2004.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Tangible Net Worth&#8221; is (i) the consolidated net worth of the Company and our consolidated subsidiaries, plus (ii) to the extent not otherwise included in such consolidated net worth, unsecured subordinated indebtedness of the Company and our consolidated subsidiaries, the terms and conditions of which are reasonably satisfactory to the required banks, minus (iii) the consolidated intangibles of the Company and our consolidated subsidiaries, including, without limitation, goodwill, trademarks, trade names, copyrights, patents, patent applications, licenses, and rights in any of the foregoing and other items treated as intangibles in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Consolidated Net Income&#8221; is the consolidated net income of the Company and our subsidiaries after deduction of all expenses, taxes, and other proper charges (but excluding any extraordinary profits or losses) determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Marketing and Sales Expenses Covenant.</font>&#160;&#160;Our ratio of marketing expenses to Vacation Interval sales for the latest rolling 12 months then ended must not equal or exceed 60% as of the last day of any fiscal quarter.&#160;&#160;One senior lender has increased such ratio to 62% as of the last day of each fiscal quarter for a four-quarter cumulative ratio.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, the ratio was 52.2% and 52.7%, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Maximum Loan Delinquency Covenant.</font>&#160;&#160;Our over 30-day delinquency rate on our entire consumer loan portfolio may not be greater than 10% as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, measured on a rolling 12 month basis based on the last day of said most recent quarter and the trailing three quarters.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, the 30-day delinquency rate was 6.3% and 6.1%, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Debt Service Covenant</font>.&#160;&#160;Our ratio of (i) earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization (&#8220;EBITDA&#8221;) less capital expenditures as determined in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles to (ii) the interest expense minus all non-cash items constituting interest expense must not be less than 1.25 to 1 as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, for the latest rolling 12 months then ending, or for the average of the last four quarters.&#160;&#160;The ratio for the latest rolling 12 months was 1.5 to 1 in each of the years ended December 31, 2009 and 2008.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Profitable Operations Covenant</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>Our Consolidated Net Income (i) for any fiscal year must not be less than $1.00, (ii) for any two consecutive fiscal quarters, determined on an individual rather than an aggregate basis, must not be less than $1.00, and (iii) for any rolling 12-month period must not be less than $1.00.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Leverage Ratio Covenant.&#160;&#160;</font>Our ratio of debt to Tangible Net Worth must not exceed 6.0 to 1 at any time during the term of the loans.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009 and 2008, the ratio was 1.9 to 1 and 1.8 to 1, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">FICO&#174; Score Covenant.&#160;&#160;</font>Our weighted average FICO&#174; Credit Bureau Score for all sales to Silverleaf Owners with respect to which a FICO&#174; score can be obtained must not be less than 640 for any fiscal calendar quarter.&#160;&#160;For the fourth quarters of 2009 and 2008, our weighted average FICO&#174; score was 688 and 697, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our credit facilities also contain covenants including requirements that we (i) preserve and maintain the collateral securing the loans; (ii) pay all taxes and other obligations relating to the collateral; and (iii) refrain from selling or transferring the collateral or permitting any encumbrances on the collateral.&#160;&#160;&#160;The credit agreements also contain restrictive covenants which include (i) restrictions on liens against and dispositions of collateral, (ii) restrictions on distributions to affiliates and prepayments of loans from affiliates, (iii) restrictions on changes in control and management of the Company, (iv) restrictions on sales of substantially all of the assets of the Company, and (v) restrictions on mergers, consolidations, or other reorganizations of the Company.&#160;&#160;Under certain credit facilities, a sale of all or substantially all of our assets, a merger, consolidation, or reorganization of the Company, or other changes of control of the Company would constitute an event of default and permit senior lenders to accelerate the maturity of the facility.</font></div>

<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We assumed that we can raise the prices on our products and services to offset costs of production as market conditions allow.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">These assumptions and estimates are subject to significant business, economic, and competitive risks and uncertainties.&#160;&#160;If our assumptions and estimates are wrong, our future results of operations and financial position may vary significantly from those projected in the business model.&#160;&#160;Our independent auditors have not reviewed or expressed an opinion about our business model or our ability to achieve it.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may be vulnerable to the current conditions in the credit markets which could adversely impact our results of operations, liquidity, and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The capital and credit markets have been experiencing unprecedented levels of volatility and disruption for more than two years.&#160;&#160;As a consequence of the recession that began in 2007, business activity across a wide range of industries in the United States faces serious difficulties due to the lack of consumer spending and the extreme lack of liquidity in the credit markets.&#160;&#160;Unemployment has also increased significantly.&#160;&#160;Because we use various mass marketing techniques, a certain percentage of our sales are generated from customers who may be considered to have marginal credit quality. During 2009 and 2008, approximately 13.7% and 14.7%, respectively, of our sales were made to customers with FICO&#174; scores below 600. In addition, we have experienced an increase in defaults in our loan portfolio as compared to historical rates. Due to current economic conditions, there can be no assurance that defaults have stabilized or that they will not increase further.&#160;&#160;These and other recent adverse changes in the credit markets and related uncertain economic conditions may eliminate or reduce the availability or increase the cost of significant sources of funding for us in the future.&#160;&#160;Specifically, if default rates for our borrowers were to continue to rise, it may require further increases in our estimated uncollectible revenue, and it could result in a default of the maximum loan delinquency covenant discussed above.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may be impacted by general economic conditions.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We anticipate a continuation of the difficult economic environment we experienced throughout 2008 and 2009.&#160;&#160;These economic weaknesses present formidable challenges related to constrained consumer spending, collection of customer receivables, access to capital markets, and ability to manage inventory levels.&#160;&#160;Our customers may be more vulnerable to deteriorating economic conditions than consumers in the luxury or upscale timeshare markets.&#160;&#160;Additionally, significant increases in the cost of transportation may limit the number of potential customers who travel to our resorts for a sales presentation.&#160;&#160;A sustained weakness or weakening in business and economic conditions generally or specifically in the principal markets in which we do business could also cause an increase in the number of our customers who become delinquent, file for protection under bankruptcy laws, or default on their loans.&#160;&#160;This could result in further increases in our provision for estimated uncollectible revenue in 2010.&#160;&#160;However, we believe that conservative business decisions and cash flow management during 2010, along with other measures in the coming year, will allow us to maintain adequate liquidity through 2010.&#160;&#160;These other measures include continuing to focus on improving the credit quality of our notes receivable, a continued favorable sales-mix trend toward upgrades and second-week sales to existing customers as such sales have relatively lower associated sales and marketing costs, reductions in capital expenditures for expansion at existing resorts, including construction of lodging units and additional amenities, negotiation of extensions to our existing credit facilities, and the management of our liquidity through business efficiencies.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance that economic conditions will not deteriorate further, which could increase customer loan delinquencies and defaults.&#160;&#160;Increases in loan delinquencies and defaults could impair our ability to pledge or sell such loans to lenders in order to obtain sufficient cash advances to meet our obligations through 2010.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may have more funds on deposit at banks than is covered by FDIC insurance limits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2009, we had substantial sums of cash on deposit with various banks.&#160;&#160;If a bank becomes insolvent and is taken over by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, we may lose cash in excess of the current insurable limits for our accounts.&#160;&#160;A loss of a significant portion of our cash would have a material impact on our ability to operate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are at risk for defaults by our customers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We offer financing to the buyers of Vacation Intervals at our resorts.&#160;&#160;Notes receivable from timeshare buyers constitute one of our principal assets.&#160;&#160;These buyers make down payments of at least 10% of the purchase price and deliver promissory notes to us for the balances.&#160;&#160;The promissory notes generally bear interest at a fixed rate, are payable over a seven-year to ten-year period, and are secured by a deed of trust on the Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;We bear the risk of defaults on these promissory notes.&#160;&#160;Although we prescreen prospects via credit scoring in the early stages of the marketing and sales process, we generally do not perform a detailed credit history review of our customers, as is the case with most other timeshare developers.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For the years ended December 31, 2009 and 2008, we recorded 33.3% and 24.6% of the purchase price of Vacation Intervals as estimated uncollectible revenue, which resulted in decreases in our sales revenue of $80.3 million and $63.1 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;When a buyer of a Vacation Interval defaults, we foreclose on the Vacation Interval and attempt to resell it.&#160;&#160;The associated marketing, selling, and administrative costs from the original sale are not recovered; and we incur such costs again when we resell the Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;Although we may have recourse against a Vacation Interval buyer for the unpaid price, certain states have laws that limit our ability to recover personal judgments against customers who have defaulted on their loans.&#160;&#160;For example, if we were to file a lawsuit to collect the balance owed to us by a customer in Texas (where approximately 52% of Vacation Interval sales occurred in 2009), the customer could file a court proceeding to determine the fair market value of the property foreclosed upon.&#160;&#160;In such event, we would only recover the amount that the indebtedness owed to us exceeds the property&#8217;s fair market value rather than the full amount owed.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we have generally not pursued this remedy.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2009, we had Vacation Interval customer notes receivable in the approximate principal amount of $449.7 million, and had an allowance for uncollectible notes of $94.6 million.&#160;&#160;Due to the current economic conditions and the deterioration of the sub-prime mortgage markets in recent years, the risk of Vacation Interval defaults has heightened.&#160;&#160;We cannot be certain that this allowance is adequate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We must borrow funds to finance our operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our business is dependent on our ability to finance customer notes receivable through our lenders.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, we either directly or through our fully consolidated finance subsidiaries owed $388.3 million of principal to our senior lenders.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Borrowing Base. </font>We have receivables-based loan agreements with senior lenders to borrow up to $364.8 million.&#160;&#160;We have pledged our customer promissory notes as security under these agreements.&#160;&#160;Our senior lenders typically lend us 75% to 80% of the principal amount of such customers' notes.&#160;&#160;Collections from Silverleaf Owners on such notes are credited directly to our senior lenders and applied against our loans receivable balances. At December 31, 2009, we had a portfolio of approximately 51,185 Vacation Interval customer notes receivable in the approximate principal amount of $449.7 million.&#160;&#160;Approximately $8.5 million in principal amount of our customer notes were 61 days or more past due and, therefore, ineligible as collateral.&#160;&#160;The amount of customer notes receivable eligible as collateral in the future may not be sufficient to support the borrowings we may require for our liquidity and continued growth.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Negative Cash Flow. </font>We ordinarily receive only 10% to 15% of the purchase price as a down payment on the sale of a Vacation Interval, but we must pay in full the cost of developing, marketing, and selling the interval.&#160;&#160;Maximum borrowings available under our credit facilities may not be sufficient to cover these costs, thereby straining our capital resources, liquidity, and capacity to grow.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest Rate Mismatch. </font>At December 31, 2009, our portfolio of customer loans receivable had a weighted average fixed interest rate of 16.8%.&#160;&#160;At such date, our borrowings (which bear interest predominantly at variable rates) against the portfolio had a weighted average cost of funds of 6.0% per annum.&#160;&#160;We have historically derived net interest income from our financing activities because the interest rates we charge our customers who finance the purchase of their Vacation Intervals exceed the interest rates we pay to our senior lenders.&#160;&#160;As 80% of our senior indebtedness bears interest at variable rates and our customer notes receivable bear interest at fixed rates, increases in interest rates will erode the spread in interest rates that we have historically experienced and could cause our interest expense on borrowings to exceed our interest income on our portfolio of customer loans.&#160;&#160;Although interest rates remained fairly constant throughout 2009, any increase in interest rates above applicable floor rates, particularly if sustained, could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, cash flows, and financial position.&#160;&#160;To the extent interest rates decrease on alternative financing sources available to our customers, we face an increased risk that customers will pre-pay their loans, which would reduce our income from operating activities.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Maturity Mismatch. </font>We typically provide financing to our customers over a seven-year to ten-year period.&#160;&#160;Our customer notes had a weighted average maturity of seven years at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Our senior credit facilities have scheduled maturity dates between June 2010 and March 2020.&#160;&#160;Additionally, should our revolving credit facilities be declared in default, the amount outstanding could be immediately due and payable.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, there could be a mismatch between our anticipated cash receipts and cash disbursements in future periods. Although we have historically been able to secure financing sufficient to fund our operations, we do not presently have agreements with our senior lenders to extend the terms of our existing funding commitments beyond their scheduled maturity dates (aside from the amendment and extension of the $106 million SF-IV facility and the extension of the $50 million inventory facility completed in the first quarter of 2010, mentioned earlier in this report) or to replace such commitments upon their expiration.&#160;&#160;If we are unable to refinance our existing loans, we could be required to sell our portfolio of customer notes receivable, probably at a substantial discount, or to seek other alternatives to enable us to continue in business.&#160;&#160;We cannot be certain that we will be able to obtain required financing in the future.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Impact on Sales.</font> Limitations on the availability of financing would inhibit sales of Vacation Intervals due to (i) the lack of funds to finance the initial negative cash flow that results from sales that we finance and (ii) reduced demand if we are unable to provide financing to purchasers of Vacation Intervals.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may not be able to obtain additional financing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Several unpredictable factors may cause our adjusted EBITDA to be insufficient to meet debt service requirements or satisfy financial covenants.&#160;&#160;We incurred a net loss in 2003.&#160;&#160;Should we record net losses in future periods, our cash flow and our ability to obtain additional financing could be materially and adversely impacted.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Many factors that determine whether or not we generate sufficient EBITDA to meet current or future debt service requirements and satisfy financial covenants are inherently difficult to predict.&#160;&#160;These factors include:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Under various federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, and regulations, as well as common law, the owner or operator of real property generally is liable for the costs of removal or remediation of certain hazardous or toxic substances located on, in, or emanating from such property, as well as related costs of investigation and property damage.&#160;&#160;Such laws often impose liability without regard to whether the owner knew of, or was responsible for, the presence of the hazardous or toxic substances.&#160;&#160;The presence of such substances, or the failure to properly remediate such substances, may adversely affect the owner's ability to sell or lease a property or to borrow money using such real property as collateral.&#160;&#160;Other federal and state laws require the removal or encapsulation of asbestos-containing material when such material is in poor condition or in the event of construction, demolition, remodeling, or renovation.&#160;&#160;Other statutes may require the removal of underground storage tanks.&#160;&#160;Noncompliance with these and other environmental, health, or safety requirements may result in the need to cease or alter operations at a property.&#160;&#160;Further, the owner or operator of a site may be subject to common law claims by third parties based on damages and costs resulting from violations of environmental regulations or from contamination associated with the site.&#160;&#160;Phase I environmental reports (which typically involve inspection without soil sampling or ground water analysis) were prepared in 2001 or later by independent environmental consultants for all of the Existing Resorts.&#160;&#160;The reports did not reveal, nor are we aware of, any environmental liability that would have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity, or financial position.&#160;&#160;We cannot be certain that the Phase I reports revealed all environmental liabilities or that no prior owner created any material environmental condition not known to us.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain environmental laws impose liability on a previous owner of property to the extent hazardous or toxic substances were present during the prior ownership period.&#160;&#160;A transfer of the property may not relieve an owner of such liability.&#160;&#160;Thus, we may have liability with respect to properties previously sold by us or by our predecessors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We believe that we are in compliance in all material respects with all federal, state, and local ordinances and regulations regarding hazardous or toxic substances.&#160;&#160;We have not been notified by any governmental authority or third party of any non-compliance, liability, or other claim in connection with any of our present or former properties.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our sales could decline if our resorts do not qualify for participation in an exchange network.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The attractiveness of Vacation Interval ownership is enhanced by the availability of exchange networks that allow Silverleaf Owners to exchange in a particular year the occupancy right in their Vacation Interval for an occupancy right in another participating network resort.&#160;&#160;According to ARDA, the ability to exchange Vacation Intervals was cited by many buyers as an important reason for purchasing a Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;Several companies, including RCI, provide broad-based Vacation Interval exchange services.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, all Existing Resorts are qualified for participation in the RCI exchange network.&#160;&#160;We cannot be certain that the Existing Resorts or any future resorts will continue to qualify for participation in these networks or any other exchange network.&#160;&#160;If such exchange networks cease to function effectively, or if our resorts are not accepted as exchanges for other desirable resorts, our sales of Vacation Intervals could decline.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have no control over RCI, and any changes in their operation could have a material impact on our Vacation Interval Owners&#8217; ability to exchange their week for one in the RCI network.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We believe the market for resale of Vacation Intervals is very limited and that resale prices are substantially below the original purchase price of a Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;This may make ownership of Vacation Intervals less attractive to prospective buyers.&#160;&#160;Owners of Vacation Intervals who wish to sell their Vacation Interval compete with our sales efforts.&#160;&#160;Vacation Interval resale clearinghouses and brokers, including Internet-based clearinghouses, do not currently have a material impact on our sales.&#160;&#160;However, if the secondary market for Vacation Intervals becomes more organized and liquid, whether through Internet-based clearinghouses and brokers or other means, the availability of resale intervals at lower prices could materially and adversely affect our prices and our ability to sell new Vacation Intervals.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our sales are seasonal in nature.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are not insured for certain types of losses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">While we believe that we maintain adequate levels of insurance for most casualties and losses, we do not insure certain types of losses (such as losses arising from floods in non-floodplain areas and acts of war) either because insurance is unavailable or unaffordable.&#160;&#160;Should an uninsured loss or a loss in excess of insured limits occur, we could be required to repair damage at our expense or lose our capital invested in a damaged resort, as well as lose anticipated future revenues from such resort.&#160;&#160;However, we would continue to be obligated on any mortgage indebtedness or other obligations related to the property.&#160;&#160;Hence, our results of operations, liquidity, and financial position could be adversely affected by such losses.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our Articles of Incorporation authorize the Board of Directors to issue up to 10,000,000 shares of preferred stock in one or more series and to establish the preferences and rights, including the right to vote and the right to convert into common stock.&#160;&#160;Such preferences and rights would likely grant such preferred stockholders certain preferences in right of payment upon a dissolution of the Company and the liquidation of our assets that would not be available to common stockholders.&#160;&#160;To the extent that our credit facilities would permit, the Board could also establish a dividend payable to the holders of the preferred stock that would not be available to common stockholders.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our cash flow may not be adequate upon an acceleration of deferred income taxes.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">While we report sales of Vacation Intervals as income at the time of the sale after receiving a 10% to 15% down payment for financial reporting purposes, we report substantially all of the Vacation Interval sales we finance under the installment method for regular federal income tax purposes.&#160;&#160;Under this method, income on sales of Vacation Intervals is not recognized until cash is received, either in the form of a down payment or as installment payments on customer notes receivable.&#160;&#160;Our liability for deferred income taxes (i.e., taxes owed to taxing authorities in the future related to income previously reported in the financial statements) was $111.2 million at December 31, 2009, primarily attributable to this method of reporting Vacation Interval sales, before utilization of any available deferred tax benefits (up to $75.9 million at December 31, 2009), including net operating loss carryforwards, limitations on the use of which are discussed below.&#160;&#160;These amounts do not include accrued interest on the deferred taxes, which will be payable if the deferred taxes become payable, the amount of which is not now reasonably ascertainable.&#160;&#160;If we should sell our installment notes or be required to factor such notes or if the notes were foreclosed on by one of our senior lenders or otherwise disposed of, the deferred gain would be reportable for regular federal tax purposes and the deferred taxes, including interest on the taxes for the period such taxes were deferred, as computed under Section 453 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;), would become due.&#160;&#160;We cannot be certain that we would have sufficient cash resources to pay those taxes and interest nor can we be certain how the payment of such taxes may affect our operational liquidity needs.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, if our sales of Vacation Intervals should decrease in the future, our diminished operations may not generate either sufficient tax losses to offset taxable income or funds to pay the deferred tax liability from prior periods.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are subject to Alternative Minimum Taxes.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For purposes of computing the 20% alternative minimum tax (&#8220;AMT&#8221;) imposed under Section 55 of the Code on our alternative minimum taxable income (&#8220;AMTI&#8221;), the installment sales method is generally not allowed.&#160;&#160;The Code requires an adjustment to our AMTI for a portion of our adjusted current earnings (&#8220;ACE&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Our ACE must be computed without application of the installment sales method.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we anticipate that we will pay AMT in future years.&#160;&#160;However, Section 53 of the Code provides for a credit (&#8220;minimum tax credit&#8221;) against our regular federal income tax liability for all or a portion of any AMT previously paid.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For 2009, we estimate our AMT liability was $3.1 million, which results in total AMT credit carryforwards of $23.3 million as of December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Our credit carryforwards as of December 31, 2008 were $20.2 million, as adjusted.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Due to the exchange offer described under the next heading, an ownership change within the meaning of Section 382(g) of the Code occurred.&#160;&#160;Under Section 383, the excess credits existing as of the date of an ownership change can be used to offset tax liability for post-change years only to the extent of the Section 383 Credit Limitation, which is defined as the tax liability attributable to taxable income to the extent it does not exceed the Section 382 limitation for such post-change year (to the extent available after the application of various adjustments).&#160;&#160;As a result of certain refunds of previously paid AMT, there is no minimum tax credit that is subject to Section 383 of the Code as a result of our ownership change.&#160;&#160;If it is subsequently determined that we have an AMT liability for prior years, and thus a minimum tax credit as of the time of the exchange offer, or if additional &#8220;ownership changes&#8221; within the meaning of Section 382(g) of the Code occur in the future, the ownership changes may result in a limitation on the use of our minimum tax credit.&#160;&#160;See the discussion under the next heading regarding possible future ownership changes.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our use of net operating loss carryforwards could be limited by an ownership change.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We had net operating loss (&#8220;NOL&#8221;) carryforwards of $143.3 million at December 31, 2009 for regular federal income tax purposes, related primarily to the immediate deduction of expenses and the simultaneous deferral of installment sale gains.&#160;&#160;In addition to the general limitations on the carryback and carryforward of NOLs under Section 172 of the Code, Section 382 of the Code imposes additional limitations on the utilization of NOLs by a corporation following various types of ownership changes which result in more than a 50 percentage point change in ownership of a corporation within a three-year period.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our completion in 2002 of our exchange offer with certain holders of our senior subordinated notes resulted in an ownership change within Section 382(g) as of May 2, 2002 (the &#8220;change date&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As a result, the future utilization of $10.9 million of our NOL as of December 31, 2009 is subject to limitation for regular federal income tax purposes.&#160;&#160;There is an annual limitation of $768,000, which was the value of our stock immediately before the ownership change, multiplied by the applicable long-term tax exempt rate.&#160;&#160;However, that annual limitation may be increased for any recognized built-in gain, which existed as of the change date to the extent allowed in Section 382 of the Code.&#160;&#160;We believe that the built-in gain associated with the installment sale gains as of the change date increases the annual limitation and will allow the utilization of most of the $10.9 million portion of our NOL as needed.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, we cannot be certain that the limitations of Section 382 will not limit or deny our future utilization of the $10.9 million portion of our NOL.&#160;&#160;Such limitation or denial could require us to pay substantial additional federal and state taxes and interest.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Moreover, we cannot be certain that future ownership changes will not limit or deny our future utilization of all of our NOL.&#160;&#160;If we cannot utilize our NOL, we will be required to pay substantial additional federal and state taxes and interest.&#160;&#160;Such tax and interest liabilities may adversely affect our liquidity.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We could be liable for back payroll taxes if our independent contractors are reclassified as employees.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Although we treat all on-site sales personnel as employees for payroll tax purposes, we do have independent contractor agreements with certain sales and marketing persons or entities.&#160;&#160;We have not treated these independent contractors as employees and do not withhold payroll taxes from the amounts paid to such persons or entities.&#160;&#160;In the event the Internal Revenue Service or any state or local taxing authority were to successfully classify such persons or entities as employees, rather than as independent contractors, we could be liable for back payroll taxes.&#160;&#160;This could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, liquidity, and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We could be negatively impacted by national and state Do-Not-Call Lists.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We rely heavily on telemarketing activities to arrange tours of our resorts to potential customers.&#160;&#160;On July 3, 2003, the Federal Communications Commission (&#8220;FCC&#8221;) released new rules and regulations promulgated under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act of 1991, which could have a negative impact on our telemarketing activities.&#160;&#160;The FCC has implemented, in conjunction with the Federal Trade Commission (&#8220;FTC&#8221;), a National Do Not Call Registry, which applies to both interstate and intrastate commercial telemarketing calls.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The FTC has reported that approximately 191 million telephone numbers had been registered on the National Do Not Call Registry as of September 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;</font>This will continue to limit the number of contacts we will be able to make through our telemarketing activities.&#160;&#160;We will continue to telemarket to individuals who do not place their telephone numbers on a do-not-call list and those with whom we have an established business relationship.&#160;&#160;Our use of autodialers to call potential customers in our database could also be restricted by new call abandonment standards specified in the FCC rules and regulations.&#160;&#160;The large quantity of telephone numbers registered on the National Do Not Call Registry and the restrictions on our use of autodialers could negatively affect our sales and marketing efforts and require us to use less effective, more expensive alternative marketing methods such as direct mail.&#160;&#160;The new rules became effective on October 1, 2003 and we have experienced a decline in the number of telemarketing calls we are able to complete as a result of the changes in the rules relating to the use of automatic dialers.&#160;&#160;All companies involved in telemarketing have experienced some negative impact to their businesses as a result of the do-not-call rules and other federal and state legislation, which seeks to protect the privacy of consumers from various types of marketing solicitations.&#160;&#160;Because of our historical dependence on telemarketing, we believe that these changes in the law will continue to have a material impact on our operations and will require us to modify our historical marketing practices in order to both remain compliant with the law and to achieve the levels of resort tours by consumers which are necessary for our profitable operation.&#160;&#160;We will continue to assess the do-not-call rules' impact on both operations and alternative methods of marketing, such as direct mail, that are not impacted by the new rules.&#160;&#160;In addition to the National Do-Not-Call List, various states have implemented Do-Not-Call legislation that also may affect our business.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Approximately 52.2% of our shares are held by non-affiliates and there has historically been a low and inconsistent trading volume for our shares.&#160;&#160;For example, the average daily trading volume for our shares for the two-month period ended February 28, 2010 was approximately 32,000&#173;&#173;&#173; shares.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that an active and steady trading market, which is not subject to extreme fluctuations, will develop for our shares.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Sales of common stock by existing shareholders, including officers or directors, may adversely affect the market price of our common stock.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Approximately 47.8% of our common stock is held by affiliates, including our executive officers and directors.&#160;&#160;Volume sales of stock by these affiliates in the trading market coupled with the historically low daily trading volume for our common stock may materially and adversely affect the market price of our common stock.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We may fail to meet the continued listing requirements of The NASDAQ Capital Market.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Effective February 28, 2007, we began trading on The NASDAQ Capital Market (&#8220;NASDAQ&#8221;) and ceased trading on AMEX.&#160;&#160;However, due to the historic volatility of the market trading price of our common stock, there can be no assurance that we will continue to meet the requirements for continued listing on NASDAQ.&#160;&#160;Our failure to comply with NASDAQ listing standards could result in the delisting of our common stock by NASDAQ, thereby limiting the ability of our shareholders to sell our common stock.&#160;&#160;During October 2008, due to market conditions, NASDAQ suspended the bid price and market value of publicly held shares requirements through January 16, 2009.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Effective January 16, 2009, the SEC extended the temporary suspension of the NASDAQ rules requiring a minimum $1 closing bid price and a minimum market value of publicly held shares through April 20, 2009.&#160;&#160;Also in January 2009, the SEC approved a NASDAQ proposal that extended the compliance period for companies that fail to meet the continued listing requirement for market value of listed securities from 30 to 90 days.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On December 29, 2009, we received notification from NASDAQ stating we are no longer in compliance with the continued listing requirements for The NASDAQ Capital Market as a result of the closing bid price per share of our common stock being below the minimum trading price of $1.00 for thirty consecutive business days.&#160;&#160;In accordance with applicable NASDAQ rules, we have a grace period of 180 calendar days (until June 28, 2010) to regain compliance with the minimum closing bid price requirement for continued listing.&#160;&#160;In order to regain compliance, our closing bid price per share must be at or above $1.00 for at least ten consecutive business days before June 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;At the end of the grace period, we may be afforded an additional grace period of 180 days provided we meet the other initial listing requirements of the NASDAQ Capital Market at that time.&#160;&#160;We intend to monitor the closing bid price of our common stock and will consider whether to implement any available options to regain compliance with the continued listing requirements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Certain of our existing shareholders have the ability to exert a significant amount of control over the Company.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of December 31, 2009, Robert E. Mead, our Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, beneficially owned approximately 24.5% of our outstanding common stock, and Bradford Whitmore and a partnership controlled by him, Grace Brothers, Ltd., beneficially owned 19.8% of our common stock.&#160;&#160;As a result, these stockholders are able to exert significant influence over the Company and its activities, including the nomination, election, and removal of our Board of Directors, the adoption of amendments to our charter documents, and the outcome of any corporate transaction or other matter submitted to our shareholders for approval, including mergers, consolidations, and the sale of all or substantially all of our assets.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Mr. Mead and Mr. Whitmore&#8217;s interests may conflict with the interests of other holders of our common stock and they may take actions affecting us with which other shareholders may disagree.&#160;&#160;For example, if Mr. Mead and Mr. Whitmore acted in concert, they may jointly decide not to enter into a transaction in which our shareholders would receive consideration for their shares that is much higher than the cost of their investment in our common stock or than the then current market price of our common stock.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Getaway Resorts</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Holiday Hills Resort. </font>Holiday Hills Resort is a resort community located in Taney County, Missouri, two miles east of Branson, Missouri.&#160;&#160;Taneycomo Lake, a popular lake for trout fishing, is approximately three miles from the resort, and Table Rock Lake is approximately ten miles from the resort.&#160;&#160;The resort is 224 miles from Kansas City and 267 miles from St. Louis.&#160;&#160;Holiday Hills Resort is heavily wooded by cedar, pine, and hardwood trees, and is favored by Silverleaf Owners seeking quality golf and nightly entertainment in nearby Branson.&#160;&#160;The resort is a mixed-use development of single-family lots, condominiums, and timeshare units.&#160;&#160;The resort has 498 existing units.&#160;&#160;We have future plans to develop approximately 500 additional units at this resort, which would yield an additional 26,000 Vacation Intervals available for sale.&#160;&#160;During 2009, we added 16 new units at this resort.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Hill Country Resort. </font>Hill Country Resort is located near Canyon Lake in the hill country of central Texas between Austin and San Antonio.&#160;&#160;Area sights and activities include water-tubing on the nearby Guadalupe River and visiting the many tourist attractions in San Antonio, such as Sea World, The Alamo, The River Walk, Fiesta Texas, and the San Antonio Zoo.&#160;&#160;The resort has 374 existing units.&#160;&#160;We have future plans to develop approximately 188 additional units at this resort, which would yield an additional 9,776 Vacation Intervals available for sale.&#160;&#160;During 2009, we added 32 new units at this resort.&#160;&#160;In 2008, we purchased approximately 8 additional acres of land that is adjacent to the existing resort.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Oak N' Spruce Resort. </font>Oak N&#8217; Spruce Resort, located in the Berkshire mountains of western Massachusetts, is approximately 134 miles west of Boston, Massachusetts, and 114 miles north of New York City.&#160;&#160;Oak N' Spruce Resort is a mixed-use development which includes a hotel and timeshare units.&#160;&#160;The resort is an active sports resort popular for hiking in the Appalachian Trail, boating, fishing, snowmobiling, and cross-country skiing.&#160;&#160;The resort has 340 existing units.&#160;&#160;We have future plans to develop approximately 10 additional units at this resort, which would yield an additional 520 Vacation Intervals available for sale.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Silverleaf&#8217;s Seaside Resort. </font>Silverleaf&#8217;s Seaside Resort is located in Galveston, Texas, approximately 50 miles south of Houston, Texas.&#160;&#160;With 635 feet of beachfront, the primary amenity at the resort is the Gulf of Mexico.&#160;&#160;The resort has 144 existing units.&#160;&#160;We have future plans to develop approximately 264 additional units at this resort, which would yield an additional 13,728 Vacation Intervals available for sale.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Orlando Breeze Resort. </font>Orlando Breeze Resort is located in Davenport, Florida, just outside Orlando, Florida, near the major tourist attractions of Walt Disney World, Sea World, and Universal Studios.&#160;&#160;The resort has 60 existing units.&#160;&#160;We plan to develop approximately 12 additional units at this resort, which would yield an additional 624 Vacation Intervals available for sale.&#160;&#160;We also own an additional 31 acres contiguous to the Orlando Breeze Resort.&#160;&#160;We have not yet finalized plans for development of this property.</font></div>
