<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">1.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NATURE OF BUSINESS</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Silverleaf Resorts, Inc., a Texas Corporation (the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;Silverleaf,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;), is in the business of marketing and selling vacation intervals (&#8220;Vacation Intervals&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Our principal activities, in this regard, consist of (i) developing and acquiring timeshare resorts; (ii) marketing and selling one-week annual and biennial Vacation Intervals to new owners; (iii) marketing and selling upgrade and additional week Vacation Intervals to existing Silverleaf owners (&#8220;Silverleaf Owners&#8221;); (iv) providing financing for the purchase of Vacation Intervals; and (v) operating timeshare resorts under management agreements.&#160;&#160;We have in-house sales, marketing, financing, and property management capabilities and coordinate the operation of our 13 owned resorts (the &#8220;Existing Resorts&#8221;) and our one hotel property, The Pinnacle Lodge, as of December 31, 2009, and the development of any new timeshare resort, including site selection, design, and construction. Sales of Vacation Intervals are marketed to individuals primarily through direct mail and telephone solicitation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Each Existing Resort has a timeshare owners&#8217; association (a &#8220;Club&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Each Club (other than Orlando Breeze) operates through a centralized organization, Silverleaf Club, to manage the Existing Resorts on a collective basis.&#160;&#160;Orlando Breeze has its own club, (&#8220;Orlando Breeze Resort Club&#8221;), which operates independently of Silverleaf Club; however, we supervise the management and operation of the Orlando Breeze Resort Club under the terms of a written agreement.&#160;&#160;Silverleaf Club has contracted with us to perform the supervisory, management, and maintenance functions at the twelve Existing Resorts that it oversees.&#160;&#160;All costs of operating these Existing Resorts, including management fees paid to the Company, are to be covered by monthly dues paid by Silverleaf Owners to their respective Clubs as well as income generated by the operation of certain amenities and revenue-producing assets at these Existing Resorts.&#160;&#160;Subject to availability of funds from the Clubs, we are entitled to a management fee to compensate us for the services provided.&#160;&#160;We evaluate the Clubs in accordance with Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) &#8220;Variable Interest Entities &#8211; Initial Measurement.&#8221;&#160;&#160;As the Clubs are not-for-profit entities, consolidation is not required.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition to Vacation Interval sales revenues, we generate revenue from interest income derived from operating activities, management fees received from Silverleaf Club, and other sources.&#160;&#160;All of the operations are directly related to the resort real estate development industry.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our consolidated financial statements as of and for the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009 reflect the operations of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Silverleaf Travel, Inc., Awards Verification Center, Inc., Silverleaf Berkshires, Inc., People Really Win Sweepstakes, Inc., Silverleaf Finance II, Inc. (&#8220;SF-II&#8221;), Silverleaf Finance IV, LLC (&#8220;SF-IV&#8221;), Silverleaf Finance V, L.P. (&#8220;SF-V&#8221;), and Silverleaf Finance VI, LLC (&#8220;SF-VI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;SF-II, SF-IV, SF-V, and SF-VI are all described in more detail in Note 8.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES SUMMARY</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Basis of Presentation &#8212; </font>The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting policies generally accepted in the United States of America and in accordance with the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Use of Estimates</font> &#8212; The preparation of these consolidated financial statements requires the use of management&#8217;s estimates and assumptions in determining the carrying values of certain assets and liabilities, the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements, and the reported amounts for certain revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160;&#160;Significant management estimates include the allowance for uncollectible notes, estimates for income taxes, and the future sales plan and estimated recoveries used to allocate certain costs to inventory phases and cost of sales.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Principles of Consolidation &#8212; </font>The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, excluding Silverleaf Finance III, LLC (&#8220;SF-III&#8221;), our wholly-owned off-balance-sheet qualified special purpose finance subsidiary, which we dissolved in October 2009.&#160;&#160;All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Timeshare Accounting Practices &#8212; </font>We follow industry specific guidance as required by FASB ASC &#8220;Real Estate &#8211; Timesharing Activities.&#8221;&#160;&#160;In general, this accounting standard provides guidance on determining revenue recognition for timeshare transactions, evaluation of uncollectibility of Vacation Interval receivables, accounting for costs of Vacation Interval sales, accounting for operations during holding periods (or incidental operations), and other accounting transactions specific to timeshare operations.</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">F-7</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Revenue and Expense Recognition (including Cost of Sales) &#8212;</font> Vacation Interval sales are primarily consummated in exchange for installment notes receivable secured by deeds of trust on each Vacation Interval sold.&#160;&#160;If development costs related to a particular project or phase are complete, we recognize related Vacation Interval sales under the full accrual method after a binding sales contract has been executed, the buyer has made a down payment of at least 10%, and the statutory rescission period has expired.&#160;&#160;If all such criteria are met yet significant development costs remain to complete the project or phase, revenues are recognized on the percentage-of-completion basis.&#160;&#160;Under this method, once the sales criteria are met, revenues are recognized proportionate to costs already incurred relative to total costs expected for the project or phase.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009,&#160;&#160;no sales were deferred related to the percentage-of-completion method.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Both of these revenue recognition methods employ the relative sales value method in determining related costs of sales and inventory applicable to each Vacation Interval sale recognized.&#160;&#160;Under the relative sales value method, a cost of sales percentage is used to apply costs to related sales as follows:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total revenues to be recognized over an entire project or phase, considering both revenues recognized to date plus estimated revenues to be recognized over future periods (considering an estimate of uncollectibility and subsequent resale of recovered Vacation Intervals), are determined.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Total costs of a project or phase, considering both costs already incurred plus estimated costs to complete the phase, if any, are determined.&#160;&#160;Common costs, including amenities, are included in total estimated costs and allocated to inventory phases that such costs are expected to benefit.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The cost of sales ratio applied to each sale represents total estimated costs as a percentage of total estimated revenues, which is specific to each inventory phase.&#160;&#160;Generally, each building type is considered a separate phase.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The estimate of total revenue for a particular phase also considers factors such as trends in uncollectibles, changes in sales mix and unit sales prices, repossessions of Vacation Intervals, effects of upgrade programs, and past and expected sales programs to sell slow-moving inventory units.&#160;&#160;At least quarterly, we evaluate the estimated cost of sales percentage applied to each sale using updated information for total estimated phase revenue and total estimated phase costs.&#160;&#160;The effects of changes in estimates are accounted for in the period in which such changes first become known on a retrospective basis, such that the balance sheet at the end of the period of change and the accounting in subsequent periods reflect the revised estimates as if such estimates had been the original estimates.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As mentioned, certain Vacation Interval sales transactions are deferred until the minimum down payment has been received.&#160;&#160;We account for these transactions utilizing the deposit method.&#160;&#160;Under this method, the sale is not recognized, a receivable is not recorded, and inventory is not relieved.&#160;&#160;Any cash received is carried as a deposit until the sale can be recognized.&#160;&#160;When these types of sales are cancelled without a refund, deposits forfeited are recognized as other income and the interest portion is recognized as interest income.&#160;&#160;This income is not significant.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also sell additional and upgraded Vacation Intervals to existing owners.&#160;&#160;Revenues are recognized on an additional Vacation Interval sale, which represents a new Vacation Interval sale treated as a separate transaction from the original Vacation Interval sale, when the buyer makes a down payment of at least 10%, excluding any equity from the original Vacation Interval purchased.&#160;&#160;Revenues are recognized on an upgrade Vacation Interval sale, which is a modification and continuation of the original sale, by including the buyer&#8217;s equity from the original Vacation Interval towards the down payment of at least 10%.&#160;&#160;Revenue recognized on upgrade Vacation Interval sales represents the difference between the upgrade sales price and traded-in sales price, while related cost of sales represents the incremental increase in the cost of the Vacation Interval purchased.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Interest income is recognized as earned.&#160;&#160;Interest income is accrued on notes receivable, net of an estimated amount that will not be collected, until the individual notes become 90 days delinquent.&#160;&#160;Once a note becomes 90 days delinquent, the accrual of interest income ceases until collection is deemed probable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Management fees for services provided to Silverleaf Club and Orlando Breeze Resort Club are recognized in the period such services are provided if collection is deemed probable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Services and other income are recognized in the period such services are provided.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Sales and marketing costs are recognized in the period incurred.&#160;&#160;Commissions, however, are recognized in the period the related revenues are recognized.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cash and Cash Equivalents &#8212; </font>Cash and cash equivalents consist of all highly liquid investments with an original maturity at the date of purchase of three months or less.&#160;&#160;Cash and cash equivalents include cash, certificates of deposit, and money market funds.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Restricted Cash</font> &#8212; Restricted cash consists of certificates of deposit, collateral for construction bonds, surety bonds, and cash reserved for payments of debt.</font></div>

<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Allowance for Uncollectible Notes </font>&#8212; Estimated uncollectible revenue is recorded at an amount sufficient to maintain the allowance for uncollectible notes at a level management considers adequate to provide for anticipated losses resulting from customers' failure to fulfill their obligations under the terms of their notes.&#160;&#160;The allowance for uncollectible notes is adjusted based upon a periodic static-pool analysis of the notes receivable portfolio, which tracks uncollectible notes for each year&#8217;s sales over the lives of the notes.&#160;&#160;Other factors considered in the assessment of uncollectibility include the aging of notes receivable, historical collection experience and credit losses, customer credit scores (FICO&#174; scores), and current economic factors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Credit losses represent three varieties as follows:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A full cancellation, whereby a customer is relieved of the note obligation and we recover the underlying inventory,</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A deemed cancellation, whereby we record the cancellation of all notes that become 90 days delinquent, net of notes that are no longer 90 days delinquent, and</font></font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A note receivable reduction that occurs when a customer trades a higher value product for a lower value product or when a portion of a customer&#8217;s note obligation is relieved.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The allowance for uncollectible notes is reduced by actual cancellations and losses experienced, including losses related to previously sold notes receivable which became delinquent and were reacquired pursuant to certain recourse obligations.&#160;&#160;Recourse on sales of customer notes receivable is governed by agreements between us and the purchasers of said notes, though we typically do not have an obligation to repurchase defaulted notes held by our financing subsidiaries.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Investment in Special Purpose Entity </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8212;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>In 2005, we consummated a securitization transaction with SF-III, which was a qualified special purpose entity (&#8220;SPE&#8221;) formed for the purpose of issuing $108.7 million of Timeshare Loan-Backed Notes Series 2005-A (&#8220;Series 2005-A Notes&#8221;) in a private placement.&#160;&#160;In connection with this transaction, we sold SF-III $132.8 million in timeshare receivables that were previously pledged as collateral under revolving credit facilities with our senior lenders and Silverleaf Finance I, Inc. (&#8220;SF-I&#8221;), our former qualified SPE which was dissolved in 2005.&#160;&#160;This transaction qualified as a sale for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;In October 2009, we exercised a cleanup call on the balance of the Series 2005-A Notes and paid off the SF-III credit facility.&#160;&#160;The total payment of $10.2 million consisted of the principal balance of the Series 2005-A Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest and other fees through October 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;We dissolved SF-III simultaneously with the execution of the cleanup call.&#160;&#160;We did not record a gain or loss as a result of the dissolution as our investment in SF-III was carried on our books at fair value.&#160;&#160;See Note 8 regarding the dissolution of SF-III.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Series 2005-A Notes were secured by timeshare receivables we sold to SF-III, without recourse, except for breaches of certain representations and warranties at the time of sale.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of an</font> agreement<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">, we continued to service these timeshare receivables and received fees for our services.&#160;&#160;</font>As such fees approximated both our internal cost of servicing such timeshare receivables and fees a third party would charge to service such receivables, the related servicing asset or liability was estimated to be insignificant.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We accounted for and evaluated the investment in our SPE in accordance with the following FASB ASC topics, as applicable: &#8220;Transfers and Servicing,&#8221; &#8220;Beneficial Interests in Securitized Financial Assets,&#8221; &#8220;Investments &#8211; Debt and Equity Securities,&#8221; and &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures.&#8221;&#160;&#160;See Note 13 for disclosures regarding the fair value measurement of the investment in our SPE.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In accordance with FASB ASC &#8220;Transfers and Servicing,&#8221; our bases for classifying SF-III as a qualified SPE were (i) SF-III was demonstrably distinct from the transferor as dissolution of the SPE would have required an affirmative vote of 100% of the SPE&#8217;s Board of Directors, one of which had to be independent, (ii) prescribed restrictions on permitted activities sufficiently limited the SPE&#8217;s authority, and (iii) financial assets transferred to the SPE were passive in nature.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Prior to the dissolution of SF-III in October 2009, the fair value of the investment in our SPE was estimated based on the present value of future cash flows we expected to receive from the notes receivable sold.&#160;&#160;At the time of dissolution, we utilized the following key assumptions to estimate the fair value of such cash flows: customer prepayment rate (including expected accounts paid in full as a result of upgrades) &#8211; 15.9% to 23.9%; expected credit losses &#8211; 16.2%; discount rate &#8211; 0% to 44.9%; base interest rate &#8211; 5.37%; and loan servicing fees &#8211; 1.75%.&#160;&#160;Our assumptions were based on experience with our notes receivable portfolio, available market data, estimated prepayments, the cost of servicing, and net transaction costs.&#160;&#160;Such assumptions were assessed quarterly and, if necessary, adjustments were made to the carrying value of the investment in our SPE on a prospective basis as a change in accounting estimate, with the amount of periodic interest accretion adjusted over the remaining life of the beneficial interest.&#160;&#160;The carrying value of the investment in our SPE represented our maximum exposure to loss regarding our involvement with our SPE.&#160;&#160;We periodically reviewed the carrying value of the investment in our SPE for impairment to ensure that the carrying value did not exceed market value.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Inventories &#8212; </font>Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or market value less cost to sell.&#160;&#160;Cost includes amounts for land, construction materials, amenities and common costs, direct labor and overhead, taxes, and capitalized interest incurred in the construction or through the acquisition of resort dwellings held for timeshare sale.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2009, the estimated costs not yet incurred but expected to complete promised amenities was $708,000.&#160;&#160;Inventory costs are allocated to cost of Vacation Interval sales using the relative sales value method, as described above.&#160;&#160;We periodically review the carrying value of our inventory on an individual project basis for impairment to ensure that the carrying value does not exceed market value.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Vacation Intervals may be reacquired as a result of (i) foreclosure (or deed in lieu of foreclosure) or (ii) trade-in associated with the purchase of an upgraded or downgraded Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;Vacation Intervals reacquired are recorded in inventory at the lower of their original cost or market value.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Land, Equipment, Buildings, and Leasehold Improvements</font> &#8212; Land, equipment (including equipment under capital lease), buildings, and leasehold improvements are stated at cost.&#160;&#160;When assets are disposed of, the cost and related accumulated depreciation are removed, and any resulting gain or loss is reflected in income for the period.&#160;&#160;Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred.&#160;&#160;Significant betterments and renewals, which extend the useful life of a particular asset, are capitalized.&#160;&#160;Depreciation is calculated for all fixed assets, other than land, using the straight-line method over the estimated useful life of the assets, which range from 3 to 20 years.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Valuation of Long-Lived Assets </font>- We assess potential impairments to our long-lived assets, including land, equipment, buildings, and leasehold improvements, whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;If circumstances require a long-lived asset be tested for possible impairment, we compare undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by an asset to the carrying value of the asset.&#160;&#160;If the carrying value of the long-lived asset is not recoverable on an undiscounted cash-flow basis, impairment is recognized to the extent that the carrying value exceeds its fair value.&#160;&#160;Fair value is determined through various valuation techniques including discounted cash-flow models, quoted market values, and third-party independent appraisals, as considered necessary.&#160;&#160;We did not recognize any impairment for our long-lived assets in the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009.&#160;&#160;On January 1, 2009, we adopted the FASB ASC &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures,&#8221; which resulted in additional disclosures for land, equipment, buildings, and leasehold improvements.&#160;&#160;See Note 13.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Prepaid and Other Assets</font> &#8212; Prepaid and other assets consist primarily of prepaid insurance, prepaid postage, commitment fees, debt issuance costs, deferred commissions, novelty inventories, deposits, collected cash in senior lender lock boxes which has not yet been applied to related loan balances, and miscellaneous receivables.&#160;&#160;Commitment fees and debt issuance costs are amortized over the lives of the related debt.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009, we <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">wrote off</font> predevelopment costs associated with potential land acquisitions of $1.0 million, $1.1 million, and $2.7 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Such costs were recorded in prepaid and other assets and were written off to operating, general and administrative expense.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Income Taxes</font> &#8212; Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method.&#160;&#160;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recorded for the future tax consequences attributable to temporary differences between the basis of assets and liabilities as recognized by tax laws and their carrying value as reported in the consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;A provision or benefit is recognized for deferred income taxes relating to such temporary differences, and is measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be settled or recovered.&#160;&#160;The effect of a change in tax rates on deferred tax assets and liabilities is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date.&#160;&#160;The effect of income tax positions are recorded only if those positions are &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; of being sustained.&#160;&#160;Recognized income tax positions are measured at the largest amount that is greater than 50% likely of being realized.&#160;&#160;Changes in recognition or measurement are reflected in the period in which the change in judgment occurs.&#160;&#160;Although we do not currently have any material charges related to interest and penalties, such costs, if incurred, are reported within the provision for income taxes.&#160;&#160;Our federal tax return includes all items of income, gain, loss, expense, and credit of SF-III, which was a non-consolidated subsidiary for reporting purposes and a disregarded entity for federal income tax purposes.&#160;&#160;We had a tax sharing agreement with SF-III.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We file U.S. federal income tax returns as well as income tax returns in various states.&#160;&#160;We are no longer subject to income tax examinations by the Internal Revenue Service for years prior to 2005, although carryforward attributes that were generated prior to 2005 may still be subject to examination.&#160;&#160;For the majority of state tax jurisdictions, we are no longer subject to income tax examinations for years prior to 2005.&#160;&#160;In the state of Texas, we are no longer subject to franchise tax examinations for years prior to 2004.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of December 31, 2009, we had no unrecognized tax benefits, and as a result, no benefits that would affect our effective income tax rate.&#160;&#160;We do not anticipate any significant changes related to unrecognized tax benefits in the next 12 months.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, we did not require an accrual for interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Derivative Financial Instruments &#8212; </font>All derivatives, whether designed as hedging relationships or not, are required to be recorded on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160;&#160;Accounting for changes in the fair value of derivatives depends on the intended use of the derivative and the resulting designation.&#160;&#160;Derivatives used to hedge exposure to changes in the fair value of an asset, liability, or firm commitment attributable to a particular risk, such as interest rate risk, are considered fair value hedges.&#160;&#160;Derivatives used to hedge exposure to variability in expected future cash flows, or other types of forecasted transactions, are considered cash flow hedges.</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">F-10</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For derivatives designated as fair value hedges, changes in the fair value of the derivative and the hedged item related to the hedged risk are recognized in earnings.&#160;&#160;For derivatives designated as cash flow hedges, the effective portion of changes in the fair value of the derivative is initially reported in other comprehensive income (outside of earnings) and subsequently reclassified to earnings when the hedged transaction affects earnings, while the ineffective portion of changes in the fair value of the derivative is recognized directly in earnings.&#160;&#160;We assess the effectiveness of each hedging relationship by comparing the changes in fair value or cash flows of the derivative hedging instrument with the changes in fair value or cash flows of the designated hedged item or transaction. For derivatives not designated as hedges, changes in the fair value are recognized in earnings.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our objective in using derivatives is to increase stability related to interest expense and to manage our exposure to interest rate movements or other identified risks.&#160;&#160;To accomplish this objective, we primarily use interest rate swaps and caps within our cash-flow hedging strategy.&#160;&#160;Interest rate swaps involve the receipt of variable-rate amounts in exchange for fixed-rate payments over the life of the agreements without exchange of the underlying principal amount.&#160;&#160;Interest rate caps provide interest rate protection above the strike rate on the cap and result in our receipt of interest payments when actual rates exceed the cap strike.&#160;&#160;We recognize changes in fair value of our derivatives in earnings.&#160;&#160;The amounts recognized for such derivatives for the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009 were not significant.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Earnings Per Share</font> &#8212; Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average common shares outstanding during the period.&#160;&#160;Earnings per share assuming dilution is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares and potentially dilutive shares outstanding during the period.&#160;&#160;The number of potentially dilutive shares is computed using the treasury stock method, which assumes that the increase in the number of common shares resulting from the exercise of stock options is reduced by the number of common shares that we could have repurchased with the proceeds from the exercise of stock options.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Outstanding stock options totaling approximately 2.0 million, 3.6 million, and 1.3 million were dilutive securities that were included in the computation of diluted earnings per share at December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;Outstanding stock options totaling 492,000, 229,000, and 2.3 million were not dilutive at December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009, respectively, because the exercise price for such options exceeded the market price for our common shares.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Stock-Based Compensation</font> &#8212; We account for stock-based compensation expense in accordance with FASB ASC &#8220;Compensation &#8211; Stock.&#8221; We recognize stock-based compensation expense for all stock options granted over the requisite service period using the fair value for these options as estimated at the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Reclassifications</font> &#8212; Certain amounts in the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2008 have been reclassified to conform to the presentation format adopted in 2009. These reclassifications have no effect on the net income or financial position previously reported.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other Recent Accounting Pronouncements &#8212;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#8211;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>FASB ASC &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221; defines fair value, establishes a market-based framework or hierarchy for measuring fair value, and expands disclosures about fair value measurements.&#160;&#160;This accounting standard is applicable whenever another accounting pronouncement requires or permits assets and liabilities to be measured at fair value.&#160;&#160;It does not expand or require any new fair value measures.&#160;&#160;In February 2008, the FASB deferred the effective date of FASB ASC &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221; for one year, from January 1, 2008 to January 1, 2009, relative to non-financial assets and liabilities that are recognized or disclosed at fair value in the financial statements on a nonrecurring basis.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, our adoption of this standard on January 1, 2008 was limited to financial assets and liabilities, which primarily affected the disclosures for the investment in our SPE and our derivative contracts as shown in Note 13.&#160;&#160;This adoption did not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&#160;&#160;On January 1, 2009, we adopted the remaining aspects of the accounting standard, which apply to our non-financial long-lived assets (land, equipment, buildings, and leasehold improvements) which are measured at fair value based on a periodic impairment assessment.&#160;&#160;This adoption resulted in additional disclosures for land, equipment, buildings, and leasehold improvements, which are included herein; however the adoption of this accounting standard for these assets did not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In April 2009, the FASB provided additional guidance for estimating fair value in accordance with FASB ASC &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221; when there is no active market or where the price inputs being used represent distressed sales.&#160;&#160;This guidance reaffirms the objective of fair value measurement, which is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction (that is, not a forced liquidation or distressed sale).&#160;&#160;It also reaffirms the need to use judgment to determine if a formerly active market has become inactive, as well as to determine fair values when markets have become inactive.&#160;&#160;This update to FASB ASC &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221; was effective prospectively for reporting periods ending after June 15, 2009.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this update in the second quarter of 2009 did not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Derivatives and Hedging</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#8211; </font>We adopted the amendment to FASB ASC &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging&#8221; on January 1, 2009.&#160;&#160;This amendment expands the disclosure requirements for derivative instruments and hedging activities.&#160;&#160;Entities are required to provide enhanced disclosures about (a) how and why an entity uses derivative instruments, (b) how derivative instruments and related hedged items are accounted for under FASB ASC &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging,&#8221; and (c) how derivative instruments and related hedged items affect an entity&#8217;s financial position, financial performance, and cash flows.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this accounting standard on January 1, 2009 did not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&#160;&#160;Disclosures regarding our derivative instruments and hedging activities are included in Note 2 and in disclosures related to interest rate risk and market risk.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interim Disclosures &#8211; Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8211; </font>We adopted the amendment to FASB ASC &#8220;Interim Disclosures about Fair Value of Financial Instruments&#8221; in the second quarter of 2009.&#160;&#160;This amendment requires the existing disclosure requirements related to the fair value of financial instruments be extended to interim periods that were previously only required in annual financial statements.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this accounting standard in the second quarter of 2009 did not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&#160;&#160;Additional disclosures were included in our Form 10-Q for both the second and third quarters of 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Subsequent Events</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic"> &#8211; </font>We adopted FASB ASC &#8220;Subsequent Events&#8221; in the second quarter of 2009.&#160;&#160;This accounting standard establishes the accounting for and disclosure of events that occur after the balance sheet date but before financial statements are issued or are available to be issued. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>It requires the disclosure of the date through which an entity has evaluated subsequent events and the basis for that date; that is, whether that date represents the date the financial statements were issued or were available to be issued. <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Consistent with the requirements of this accounting standard for public entities, we evaluate subsequent events through the date the financial statements are issued.&#160;&#160;FASB ASC &#8220;Subsequent Events&#8221; should not result in significant changes in the subsequent events that an entity reports, either through recognition or disclosure, in its financial statements.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this accounting standard in the second quarter of 2009 did not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&#160;&#160;The FASB amended this accounting guidance in March 2010, effective immediately, to exclude public entities from the requirement to disclose the date on which subsequent events have been evaluated.&#160;&#160;In addition, the amendment modified the requirement to disclose the date on which subsequent events have been evaluated in reissued financial statements to apply only to such statements that have been restated to correct an error or to apply U.S. GAAP retrospectively.&#160;&#160;As a result of this amendment, we did not disclose the date through which we evaluated subsequent events in this report on Form 10-K.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Accounting for Transfers of Financial Assets &#8211; </font>In June 2009, the FASB issued FASB ASC &#8220;Accounting for Transfers of Financial Assets,&#8221; which (i) eliminated the concept of a qualified SPE, (ii) clarified the derecognition criteria for a transfer to be accounted for as a sale, (iii) clarified the unit of account eligible for sale accounting, and (iv) required that a transferor initially measure at fair value and recognize all assets obtained (for example beneficial interests) and liabilities incurred as a result of a transfer of an entire financial asset or group of financial assets accounted for as a sale.&#160;&#160;Additionally, on and after the effective date, existing qualified SPEs (as defined under previous accounting standards) must be evaluated for consolidation by reporting entities in accordance with the applicable consolidation guidance.&#160;&#160;FASB ASC &#8220;Accounting for Transfers of Financial Assets&#8221; further requires enhanced disclosures, including a transferor&#8217;s continuing involvement with transfers of financial assets accounted for as sales, the risks inherent in the transferred financial assets that have been retained, and the nature and financial effect of restrictions on the transferor&#8217;s assets that continue to be reported in the statement of financial position.&#160;&#160;This accounting standard will be effective as of the beginning of interim and annual reporting periods that begin after November 15, 2009.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this standard will not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, and cash flows as we exercised a cleanup call on the balance of the Series 2005-A Notes previously sold by SF-III effective October 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;The cleanup call resulted in the dissolution of SF-III.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities </font>&#8211; In June 2009, the FASB issued FASB ASC &#8220;Amendments to FASB ASC - Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities.&#8221;&#160;&#160;This amendment changes the consolidation guidance applicable to SPEs.&#160;&#160;It also amends the guidance governing the determination of whether an enterprise is the primary beneficiary of an SPE and therefore required to consolidate the SPE by requiring a qualitative analysis rather than a quantitative analysis.&#160;&#160;The qualitative analysis includes, among other things, consideration of who has the power to direct the activities of the entity that most significantly impact the entity&#8217;s economic performance and who has the obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits of the SPE that could potentially be significant to the SPE.&#160;&#160;This accounting standard further requires continuous reassessments of whether an enterprise is the primary beneficiary of an SPE, whereas such reassessments were previously required only when specific events had occurred.&#160;&#160;In addition, qualified SPEs, which were previously exempt from the application of FASB ASC &#8220;Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities,&#8221; will be subject to the provisions of this amendment.&#160;&#160;The amendment also requires enhanced disclosures about an enterprise&#8217;s involvement with an SPE.&#160;&#160;This accounting standard will be effective as of the beginning of interim and annual reporting periods that begin after November 15, 2009.&#160;&#160;The adoption of this standard on January 1, 2010, will not impact our consolidated financial position, results of operations, and cash flows as we have 100% ownership in our fully-consolidated SPEs (SF-II, SF-IV, SF-V, and SF-VI).&#160;&#160;In addition, we exercised a cleanup call on the balance of the Series 2005-A Notes previously sold to SF-III, our wholly-owned off-balance-sheet special purpose finance subsidiary, effective October 30, 2009, which resulted in the dissolution of SF-III.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">3.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">CONCENTRATIONS OF RISK</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">General -</font> Interest on our notes receivable portfolio, senior subordinated debt, capital leases, and miscellaneous notes is fixed, whereas interest on our primary loan agreements, which had a total facility amount of $439.5 million at December 31, 2009, have a fixed-to-floating debt ratio of 20% fixed to 80% floating.&#160;&#160;However, the majority of our floating-rate debt is subject to interest-rate floors between 5.25% and 8.00%.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At December 31, 2009, the carrying value of our notes receivable portfolio approximates fair value because the weighted average interest rate on the portfolio approximates current interest rates received on similar notes.&#160;&#160;Our fixed-rate notes receivable are subject to interest rate risk and will decrease in fair value if market rates increase, which may negatively impact our ability to sell our fixed-rate notes in the marketplace.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Credit Risk </font>&#8212; We are exposed to credit risk related to our notes receivable.&#160;&#160;We offer financing to the buyers of Vacation Intervals at our resorts.&#160;&#160;These buyers generally make a down payment of 10% to 15% of the purchase price and deliver a promissory note to us for the balance.&#160;&#160;The promissory notes generally bear interest at a fixed rate, are payable over a seven to ten year period, and are secured by a deed of trust on the Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;We bear the risk of defaults on these promissory notes.&#160;&#160;Although we prescreen prospects via credit scoring techniques in the early stages of the marketing and sales process, we generally do not perform a detailed credit history review of our customers.&#160;&#160;Due to the state of the economy in general, and related deterioration of the residential real estate market and sub-prime mortgage markets, the risk of Vacation Interval defaults has heightened.&#160;&#160;Because we use various mass-marketing techniques, a certain percentage of our sales are generated from customers who may be considered to have marginal credit quality.&#160;&#160;In addition, we have experienced an increase in defaults in our loan portfolio as compared to historical rates.&#160;&#160;Due to existing economic conditions, there can be no assurance that defaults have stabilized or will not increase further.&#160;&#160;Customer default levels, other adverse changes in the credit markets, and related uncertain economic conditions may eliminate or reduce the availability or increase the cost of significant sources of funding for us in the future.&#160;&#160;We increased our estimated uncollectible revenue as a percentage of Vacation Interval sales to 33.3% for 2009 from 24.6% for 2008.&#160;&#160;However, if default rates for our borrowers were to continue to rise, it may require an additional increase in our estimated uncollectible revenue.&#160;&#160;We will continue to evaluate our collections process and marketing programs with a view toward establishing procedures aimed at reducing note defaults and improving the credit quality of our customers.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance that these efforts will be successful.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If a buyer of a Vacation Interval defaults, we generally must foreclose on the Vacation Interval and attempt to resell it; the associated marketing, selling, and administrative costs from the original sale are not recovered; and such costs must be incurred again to resell the Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;Although in many cases we may have recourse against a Vacation Interval buyer for the unpaid note balance, certain states have laws that limit our ability to recover personal judgments against customers who have defaulted on their loans.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we have generally not pursued this remedy.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Interest Rate Risk &#8212;</font> We have historically derived net interest income from our financing activities because the interest rates we charge our customers who finance the purchase of their Vacation Intervals exceed the interest rates we pay to our senior lenders.&#160;&#160;As 80% of our senior indebtedness bears interest at variable rates and our customer notes receivable bear interest at fixed rates, increases in interest rates will erode the spread in interest rates that we have historically experienced and could cause our interest expense on borrowings to exceed our interest income on our portfolio of customer loans.&#160;&#160;Although interest rates remained fairly constant throughout 2009, any increase in interest rates above applicable floor rates, particularly if sustained, could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, cash flows, and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A hypothetical one-point interest rate increase in the marketplace at December 31, 2009 would result in a fair value decrease of approximately $14.8 million on our notes receivable portfolio.&#160;&#160;The impact of a one-point effective interest rate change on the $308.8 million balance of variable-rate debt instruments at December 31, 2009 would be approximately $688,000 on our results of operations, after income taxes, for the year ended December 31, 2009, or approximately $0.02 per diluted common share.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">To partially offset potential increases in interest rates, we have executed two interest rate swaps related to our conduit loan with SF-II, with fixed rates of 7.04% and 7.90%, for a total notional amount of $3.2 million at December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Such interest rate swaps relate to agreements that expire between September 2011 and March 2014.&#160;&#160;Our variable funding note (&#8220;VFN&#8221;) with SF-IV also acts as an interest rate hedge since it contains a provision for an interest rate cap.&#160;&#160;The balance outstanding under this line of credit at December 31, 2009 was $111.8 million.&#160;&#160;In February 2010, the maturity date of such VFN was extended to February 2013, as discussed in Note 17, &#8220;Subsequent Events.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Availability of Funding Sources &#8212; </font>We fund substantially all of our notes receivable, timeshare inventories, and land inventories which we originate or purchase with borrowings through our financing facilities, sales of notes receivable, internally generated funds, and proceeds from public debt and equity offerings.&#160;&#160;Borrowings are in turn repaid with the proceeds we receive from collections on such notes receivable.&#160;&#160;To the extent that we are not successful in maintaining or replacing existing financings, we would have to curtail our operations or sell assets, which would have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, cash flows, and financial position.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Geographic Concentration &#8212;</font> Our notes receivable and Vacation Interval inventories are primarily originated in Texas, Missouri, Illinois, Massachusetts, Georgia, and Florida.&#160;&#160;Risks inherent in such concentrations are:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">regional and general economic stability, which affects property values and the financial stability of the borrowers, and</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">

<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;</font></font></div>

<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">the continued popularity of our resort destinations, which affects the marketability of our products and the collection of notes receivable.</font></div>
</td>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">4.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">NOTES RECEIVABLE</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We provide financing to the purchasers of Vacation Intervals in the form of notes receivable, which are collateralized by their interest in such Vacation Intervals.&#160;&#160;Such notes receivable generally have initial terms of seven to ten years.&#160;&#160;The weighted average yield on outstanding notes receivable at December 31, 2008 and 2009 was 16.7% and 16.8%, respectively, with individual rates ranging from 0% to 17.5%.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2009, $3.8 million of timeshare notes receivable have interest rates below 10%.&#160;&#160;In connection with the sampler program, we routinely enter into notes receivable with terms of 10 months.&#160;&#160;Notes receivable from sampler sales were $2.5 million and $3.1 million at December 31, 2008 and 2009, respectively, and are non-interest bearing.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Once a note becomes 90 days delinquent, the accrual of interest income ceases until collection is deemed probable. We ceased accruing interest on delinquent notes of $53.2 million and $59.9 million as of December 31, 2008 and 2009, respectively, as collection of interest on such notes was deemed improbable.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There were no notes sold with recourse during the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In October 2009, we exercised a cleanup call on the balance of the Series 2005-A Notes previously sold by SF-III, </font>our former wholly-owned off-balance-sheet qualified special purpose finance subsidiary, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">and paid off the SF-III credit facility.&#160;&#160;We dissolved SF-III simultaneously with the execution of this transaction.&#160;&#160;See Note 8 regarding the dissolution of SF-III.&#160;&#160;</font>The Series 2005-A Notes were secured by timeshare receivables we sold to SF-III, without recourse, except for breaches of certain representations and warranties at the time of sale.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the terms of an<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> agreement</font>, we serviced these timeshare receivables and received fees for our services equal to 1.75% of eligible timeshare receivables held by the facility.&#160;&#160;Such fees were $854,000, $491,000, and $239,000 for the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Except for the repurchase of notes that failed to meet initial eligibility requirements, we were not obligated to repurchase defaulted or any other contracts sold to SF-III.&#160;&#160;As the servicer of notes receivable sold to SF-III, we were obligated to foreclose upon Vacation Intervals securing defaulted note receivables.&#160;&#160;Although we were not obligated, we could purchase foreclosed Vacation Intervals for net fair market value, which could not be less than fifteen percent of the original acquisition price that the customer paid for the Vacation Interval.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2007, 2008, and 2009, we paid $1.2 million, $639,000, and $1.1 million, respectively, to repurchase the Vacation Intervals securing defaulted contracts to facilitate the re-marketing of those Vacation Intervals.</font></div>

<td valign="bottom" width="1%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">$</font></td>
<td valign="bottom" width="9%" style="BORDER-BOTTOM: black 4px double; TEXT-ALIGN: right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">76,696</font></font></td>
<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>

<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px; TEXT-ALIGN: left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The provision for estimated uncollectible revenue as a percentage of Vacation Interval sales increased substantially from 24.6% for 2008 to 33.3% for 2009.&#160;&#160;As cancellations during the year 2009 exceeded cancellations projected under our static-pool analysis of our notes receivable portfolio, which tracks uncollectible notes for each year&#8217;s sales over the lives of the notes, we projected this trend to continue for the near term.&#160;&#160;Considering an increase in future cancels beyond that previously estimated, we increased our allowance for uncollectible notes by $18.5 million in the third quarter of 2009, above the 25.9% provision rate we had estimated in prior months.&#160;&#160;Factors considered in the assessment of uncollectibility include the aging of notes receivable, historical collection experience and credit losses, customer credit scores (FICO&#174; scores), and current economic factors.&#160;&#160;We believe our notes receivable are adequately reserved at this time, however, there can be no assurance that defaults have stabilized or that they will not increase further.&#160;&#160;We review the allowance for uncollectible notes quarterly and make adjustments as necessary.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The allowance for uncollectible notes as a percentage of gross notes receivable was 19.3% and 21.0% as of December 31, 2008 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;We will continue to evaluate our collections process and marketing programs with a view toward establishing procedures aimed at reducing note defaults and improving the credit quality of our customers.&#160;&#160;However, there can be no assurance that these efforts will be successful.</font></div>
